assessment_scope: Current snapshot for all six filter-response records at registry 0.2.0. The four previously assessed records are reproduced unchanged; low shelf and high shelf receive conservative initial assessments against EV-050 through EV-057 and EV-060 through EV-065.

semantic_stability.basis: EV-003 and EV-018 establish high-pass semantics, while current vendor usage documents both High-pass and Low Cut treatments. DA-003 shows that Low Cut is used for high-pass behavior but does not establish exact equivalence in every intended context; EV-024 preserves terminology divergence.

artifact_refs.claim: Supports the observed High-pass and Low Cut terminology treatments without resolving a universal exact-alias rule.

limitations: The exact Low Cut alias boundary remains material and open.

independent_usage.basis: EV-002 directly documents one compact target selector and EV-003 independently grounds the semantics. DA-003 documents further selector/control and graph contexts, but explicitly does not establish that those graphics are standalone or axis-free, so they are not counted as a second target implementation.

artifact_refs.claim: Classifies current vendor representations and prevents contextual controls from being over-counted as axis-less target implementations.

limitations: This is one point lower than the 0.1.1 snapshot because the accepted target-representation definition requires two qualifying target uses for score 3; the newer matrix makes the missing second axis-less use explicit.

text_and_accessibility.basis: High-pass filter and HPF are independently and unambiguously used in non-UI education, documentation, and trade prose, grounding the canonical term, fallback, and speech label even though no response glyph is portable plain text.
limitations: EV-023 records user confusion between high-pass and low-pass names; score 3 means actual source use is unambiguous, not that every reader is error-free.

visual_convergence.basis: EV-002 supplies one compact target selector. DA-003 and DA-002 document additional contextual controls, graphs, and historical diagrams but do not prove a second independent axis-less rendering converging on a defined primitive.

artifact_refs.claim: Classifies historical evidence as labeled, axis-bearing, or embedded context rather than standalone glyph lineage.
Shows current visual evidence remains contextual and heterogeneous.

limitations: No second independently documented axis-less target contour is established.

overlap_audit.basis: DA-005 reproducibly audits Unicode 17 semantic candidates, visual near-misses, plausible sequences, and IEC 60617 terminology using the registered primary inputs, and records explicit non-equivalence and exclusions.

artifact_refs.claim: Supplies the complete reproducible overlap and confusability audit required for score 3.

limitations: The audit excludes later Unicode versions, restricted IEC sheets, IEC 60417, ISO 7000, and font-by-font behavior.

legal_provenance.basis: Every cited ledger source has a rights note, no third-party artwork is imported, and the repository publishes no claimed reference artwork asset.

counterevidence.description: Current and historical sources often communicate the concept with text, axes, or rich UI context rather than a standalone glyph.

artifact_refs.claim: Preserves negative historical findings.
Preserves current representation heterogeneity.

semantic_stability.basis: Independent product, implementation, historical, education, trade, and community sources support a sign-agnostic low-frequency-side shelf concept. Exact alias treatment for low shelving filter remains open.
limitations: Hybrid implementations and the shelf-versus-shelving alias disposition prevent a maximal score.

independent_usage.basis: Multiple independent organizations and authors use low shelf as a filter type across product documentation, an implementation specification, education, trade media, historical documentation, and community discussion. Project reports summarize these sources but are not counted as additional evidence.
limitations: Broad semantic usage does not establish portable glyph usage or one common contour.

text_and_accessibility.basis: The full term low shelf is independently used in education, trade, product, and community prose, supporting LOW SHELF and low-shelf filter without relying on unsupported abbreviations.
limitations: LS and LSF are not established as portable, unambiguous fallbacks.

visual_convergence.basis: EV-052 and EV-054 document compact type selectors, but the evidence does not establish shared axis-less geometry or a reproducible sign-agnostic primitive.
limitations: Contextual product selectors cannot be treated as convergent standalone glyphs or reused as artwork.

overlap_audit.basis: No shelf-specific reproducible Unicode, sequence, visual-confusable, or adjacent-standard overlap audit has been completed.
limitations: The four-record overlap audit does not cover low shelf.

legal_provenance.basis: All cited ledger entries record rights limitations, no third-party artwork is imported, and no shelf artwork is accepted or published by this record.

counterevidence.description: Curve orientation alone can describe either low-side boost or high-side attenuation, so the affected side is not recoverable from every unlabelled curve.
